transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lucia Gomez (Redwood SE), Carla Hughes (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Aurion Head of AI), Tom Becker (Aurion CTO), Priya Nair (Aurion DevOps), Ethan Lo (Aurion Data Eng)

---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining the Q4 QBR for Aurion Health, appreciate you all making time. quick round robin?
[00:08] Marta: Thanks Samir, Marta here. we just wrapped a model retrain last week, so excited to sync on production metrics.
[00:15] Tom: Tom here, will join for SRE/infra questions.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, DevOps. I'll be owning the traces and infra follow-ups.
[00:22] Samir: Great, I'll hand it over to Lucia to run through the usage and reliability summary we prepared.
[00:27] Lucia: Cool thanks. so we pulled last 90 days of usage. quick highlights: average tokens per month ~ 36M, tail at peak day about 2.1M tokens, peak QPS observed in production testing was around 48 rps, p95 latency for hosted endpoints ~ 210ms for the 1k context tests we ran in sept, and error rate has been ~0.6% with most tied to transient network timeouts.
[00:52] Ethan: small note the 1k tests were synthetic, our real chats often hit 2.5k context which explains some higher latencies.
[00:58] Lucia: totally — we'll include the 2.5k traces in the benchmark. also saw opportunity for batching and prefix caching — could reduce token cost by 12-18% for your call pattern.
[01:12] Marta: can you explain the batching impact? we worry about latency tradeoffs.
[01:16] Lucia: yeah so continuous batching groups small concurrent requests to improve GPU utilization; with workload-aware policies we keep SLOs — ex: during off-peak we can batch more aggressively; at peak we switch to latency-first routing. we've got examples in the Optimize suggestions doc I shared.
[01:33] Tom: on SLOs: we need 99.9% uptime and p95 latency <250ms for key routes otherwise the clinical workflows complain. are those realistic on hosted?
[01:42] Samir: good question. hosted can hit those SLOs for standard routes — for stricter guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private, which give you reserved capacity and region pinning. Dedicated also gives autoscale policies and burst capacity.
[01:53] Priya: private deployment is attractive but will Aurion still get the same console observability and rollouts?
[01:58] Lucia: yes — Private ships with the same control plane experience, we support VPC peering or on-prem package, and you keep the same rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic fallback). only difference is the control plane endpoint is customer-managed.
[02:10] Marta: security side — for our internal audit we need SOC 2 artifacts, SSO/SAML setup, KMS integration for key management, and proof of no data leakage to third-party logs. do you have those?
[02:22] Carla: yes we have a SOC 2 report and ISO artifacts, and a SSO SAML guide. for KMS we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations on Private. i can share the security pack after this call.
[02:33] Marta: perfect, please include retention controls and audit log export examples.
[02:37] Carla: will do.
[02:39] Lucia: back to cost — your current spend in hosted the last 30 days was about $18k, mostly generation tokens. with a Dedicated reserved 6-month commit we estimate comparable throughput at ~28% lower unit cost depending on commit level and quantization. main levers: batching, quantization (we recommend 4-bit for production where acceptable), and prefix cache hit rates.
[02:58] Tom: how invasive is quantization for quality? our clinicians are picky.
[03:02] Lucia: it depends on model and evals. we run eval suites against your prompt set; for some model families 4-bit is transparent, for others there's a slight drop. we couple quantization with canary rollouts and quality monitoring so any regression is detected and auto-rolled back.
[03:18] Marta: can you run that eval for our clinical prompt set?
[03:21] Lucia: yes that's part of the benchmark deliverable. we'll run qualitative metrics and your acceptance criteria.
[03:26] Ethan: also want to validate cold-start behavior for KV cache and warm-up times for longer sequences.
[03:31] Lucia: noted — we'll include KV cache warm-up in the latency tests.
[03:34] Samir: on timeline — if we get traces by 12/09 we can run benchmarks and share results by 12/14, then you can decide whether to pilot Dedicated in Jan.
[03:44] Priya: timeline sounds ok. one question: if we go Private on-prem, what's the rollout support window?
[03:50] Carla: enterprise plan includes hands-on deployment support, runbook handover, and 3 months of priority incident support. we can extend as needed.
[03:58] Tom: what's the typical incident cadence for customers at our scale? we want to set expectations.
[04:03] Lucia: most enterprise customers see 1-2 P1s/year, many of which are due to upstream infra events. we have cross-region fallback and automatic model variant switch to keep customers online — that's reduced observed downtime in prior incidents.
[04:17] Marta: curious about routing — can we route by region and cost tier? we sometimes prefer lower-cost fallback for non-clinical background jobs.
[04:24] Lucia: absolutely. policy-based routing supports region, latency, and cost tiers. you can mark routes as clinical (latency-first) and background (cost-first); routing rules then enforce preferred model variants.
[04:35] Samir: quick commercial note — we can structure a pilot: 3-month Dedicated eval with a 20% credit back if SLA targets are missed. I'll put that in the pricing doc.
[04:45] Tom: that helps. also want engineering access to per-token breakdowns and trace-level debugging.
[04:50] Carla: Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns and we can enable trace export to your logging backend for deeper debugging.
[04:58] Marta: ok let's recap next steps.
[05:02] Samir: recap: 1) Aurion provides sample workload traces and peak QPS by 12/09 (Priya). 2) Redwood runs benchmarks (2 sequence lengths incl. 2.5k) and evals against clinical prompts, share by 12/14 (Lucia). 3) Samir sends updated pricing and pilot contract by 12/10. 4) Carla shares security pack (SOC2, SAML guide, KMS notes) by 12/11.
[05:20] Priya: noted.
[05:21] Marta: thanks everyone. one more ask: please include an example runbook for canary rollback for our compliance team.
[05:28] Carla: will include a runbook example in the security pack.
[05:31] Samir: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive. thanks all.
[05:36] Tom: thanks.
[05:38] Marta: thanks, bye.

---
Notes:
- References: Optimize suggestions doc (link shared in chat), security pack (to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (to be created by Lucia).
- Transcript contains occasional short overlaps and filler; some product names were auto-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> K V cache).

End of transcript.
